ar3.justification: RI-UIX05 §Seam declares the piece 'Not sterile' on the strength of R3's exception: reading a book adds a dialogue topic, and under S13 a topic can be a parley key that ends a fight without a corpse. Measured in the running engine, that crossing does not exist. 60 of 65 books declare topics_taught (116 distinct topics); `topics_taught` is read by no file in game/src/; opening all 60 in the engine leaves topicsKnown as []. The second declared crossing — a book unlocking a non-violent quest resolution through requires.knowledge — is equally dead (see CONSUMPTION). The piece therefore carries ZERO boundary-crossing interactions and is reported as sterile rather than failed, per ARBITRATION §3.

consumption.demonstration: Drove all three knowledge-gated non-violent resolutions in a real browser. Opened all 60 topic-teaching books: topicsKnown [] before, [] after, 0 gained.

biggest_gap.what: 37,819 words in 65 texts open 65/65 in the engine across 324 pages, and the only thing a player can do with any of it is read it. Both mechanical consumers the two items name are dead code. (1) `book.knowledge_key` is read by no file in game/src/; the three non-violent quest resolutions that gate on those keys — Q-SOUL-02 res_seal, Q-LILM-01 res_rootkeepers, Q-DEEP-01 res_broker — are unreachable by any route in the shipped build, and the engine reports the identical refusal before and after the book has been opened and read to the last page. (2) `book.topics_taught` (60 books, 116 topics) is read by nothing; opening all 60 in the engine leaves topicsKnown empty. That field is RI-UIX05 R3's permitted exception and the item's entire declared AR-3 seam crossing.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: RI-UIX05 §D's last row exists, in the item's own words, because 'a player who read the right book three regions ago knows a name, and a name is a parley key (S13) or a topic (R3's exception) ... this row owns whether the reading surface is connected to anything.' It reports 17 by reading JSON and 0 by asking the game. Three of the build's non-violent exits are closed, which pushes against the >=45% non-combat resolution bar; and the piece's only route across the Souls/Morrowind seam does not exist. ARBITRATION §3 CONSUMPTION is explicit that a model with no demonstrated consumer scores 0 exactly as a missing model does, because from the player's chair they are the same thing.

remedy.summary: Fire one callback from the book-open path into the quest engine, so that reading a book writes what the book says it teaches.
steps: In game/src/ui/system.js, in the open('book', {id}) branch that already resolves the book record (around line 129), on FIRST open of a given book id call a new questEngine.readBook(bookRecord).

readBook(): for each t in book.topics_taught, append through game/src/sim/quest/topic-supply.js's fold-safe appender into sim.quest.topicsKnown — that module exists and is already the correct door, and it dedupes on the folded key.

readBook(): if book.knowledge_key is set, add it to a new sim.quest.booksRead Set, and union that Set into ctx.knowledge at game/src/sim/quest/machine.js:142. One line at each site; no quest data changes.
Add sim.quest.booksRead to the save manifest, or a load silently closes the doors again (this is the W1-SAVE lesson: audit the live world after the load, not the bytes).

Guard against R3/R4: a topic is a NAME, never a destination. Nothing may be written to the journal, no marker may be created, and RI-UIX02's quest-state differential must show no on-screen change outside the book.
remedy.acceptance_test: node tools/harness/critic-w1-library-consume.mjs must report available:false in the control and available:true (or a `why` array that no longer contains 'you have not learned book_*') after reading, for all three cases; node tools/harness/critic-w1-library-seam.mjs must report a non-empty topics_gained_by_reading_every_book. Both probes exist and both currently go red.
remedy.estimated_size: small — two call sites and a save field

secondary_observations.what: THE TELL IS ONE WORD. 'eleven' appears in 49 of our 65 books (75.4%), 120 times, 31.73 per 10k words. In 241 real Morrowind/Tribunal/Bloodmoon books it appears in 7 (2.9%), 7 times, 0.38 per 10k words — an 84x per-word rate. It is in an Imperial surveyor's expense claim, an Argonian keeper's leave book, a children's counting rhyme, a toll receipt and a Bravil romance alike. 'nineteen years' appears in two unrelated books as the length of a career. The remedy is a lexical de-duplication pass over the numerals, not a rewrite; the prose itself is excellent.

RI-LOR03 §1 IS NOW MEASURABLE AND SHOULD BE AMENDED. tools/uesp/mw-book-stats.py recovers 241 shipped Morrowind/Tribunal/Bloodmoon books with full text from the vendored UESP extract. Measured against the recalled table: median 535 vs ~520 (good), p90 1673 vs ~1700 (good), max 4090 vs ~4500 (good), mean 770 vs ~700 (good) — but p10 165 vs ~90, p25 299 vs ~210 and p75 1125 vs ~960 are all materially low, and Morrowind's real short tail is 8.7% under 150 words against our 16.9%. The item's own provenance note asks for exactly this amendment, keeping the old figures struck through.

ONE OF THE 24 CONTRADICTION PAIRS IS A NEAR-COPY OF ITS PARTNER. a-progress-ii and pilots-chart-book share 5.36% of their 7-grams and give the SAME landmark order, the SAME left ear and the SAME distances. All three errors declared in a-progress-ii's wrong_on_purpose field are absent from the prose, and the third is contradicted by the game's own dialogue (game/data/dialogue/rumours.json:75 ships an archon-crane). The joke — a plagiarist who reversed his direction and did not notice — is in the metadata and not in the book. a-progress-iii, by contrast, genuinely contains its declared errors (snow in Thornmarsh, a hatching at noon, a doorway on the fourth terrace).

K1 IS NOT UNSATISFIABLE AND NO AMENDMENT IS WARRANTED. p10 >= 80 fails at 62.3 because 13 books end on a page under 25 words, including a 3-word page. A last-page balancing pass — §A B8's own orphan/widow requirement — over the same page counts lifts p10 to 82.3 with p90 152.7. The residual (median 119 against a 120 floor) is recovered by raising page capacity, which runs at median 126 against an observed max of 172.

p90 = 1264 PASSES ONLY ON THE TOOL'S PERCENTILE CONVENTION. book-stats.py's pct() uses a floor-index estimator; linear interpolation (numpy's and statistics.quantiles' default) gives 1134.8 against a 1200 bar. The same estimator decides step 6's IQR, which passes at 6.15 against a bar of 6.0. Two of the item's rows are inside their bars by a choice of estimator.

SIX OF RI-UIX05'S TEN CHECKS HAVE BEEN RUN BY NOBODY. K2 (line length, leading, size at three resolutions), K3 (contrast), K5 (open and turn latency), K6 (T5 persistence across save/load), K7 (pause rule in and out of combat) and K10 (art-neutralised layout blind pair). tools/analysis/text-metrics.mjs has never been pointed at the reading screen. This is not the library builder's debt but it is why the item cannot be closed.

RI-UIX05 §C's PROHIBITION SCAN SHOULD BE SCOPED TO ELEMENT KINDS, NOT PAGE TEXT. The builder reworded three books because their prose contained the words 'summary' and 'skip' — 'PREFACE, WHICH THE READER WILL SKIP' is a joke in a book, not a UI affordance. Rewording fiction to satisfy a UI scanner is the wrong direction of causation and the next library will hit it again. Step 6 should read getUIState().elements[].kind, not .text.

book-stats.py S4a compares a count of BOOKS (33) against contradiction_pairs_min, which RI-LOR03 states as >= 8 PAIRS. The label and the value disagree and the check is looser than the item. Immaterial at 24 pairs; a defect nonetheless.

WHAT IS GENUINELY GOOD AND MUST SURVIVE A FIX: eight book ids that shipped quests already required and that did not exist are now written; three sealed-mystery evidence books exist and --leak-scan is CLEAN over 2,607 strings (re-run by this critic); CF-D004 and CF-D006 had no in-world source anywhere in the game and now have both sides; an id collision on what-the-water-took was caught, which would have made one of two books silently unreachable through the engine's Map. The --compare argument really does parse RI-LOR03's own tables rather than decorate the command line. Sentence for sentence the library is better than the corpus it imitates.

gap_closure.note: The ratio is real and the denominator is confirmed (1,231 words of item `description` across 44 records). But K9 is a six-row check and it fails on the row the item itself calls decisive: books readable before the quest that references them reports 17 on disk and 0 in the running world. The headline number moved and the check did not pass.

method_deviations.deviation: Wrote tools/uesp/mw-book-stats.py — extracts and measures Morrowind's own book corpus (241 texts with recoverable full text out of 483 shipped {{Game Book}} pages) from corpus/uesp_morrowind_blackmarsh_extract.jsonl.xz, reports the length distribution under two percentile conventions, dumps one plaintext file per book for blind packs, and counts numeral-token frequencies for the one-author test.
method_deviations.why: RI-LOR03 §1 is provenance: canonical-recall and its own provenance note invites re-measurement if anyone can extract the game's BOOK records. Nobody had. Without it there is no reference distribution to compare ours against and no baseline for the numeral tic, which is the finding that decides step 2.

method_deviations.deviation: Ran RI-LOR03 step 2 with a PRE-REGISTERED ARITHMETIC RULE in place of a human judgement, and recorded the blind protocol itself as void.
method_deviations.why: RI-MTH03 M2 requires a judge with no knowledge of which side is which; this critic built the packs and no fresh-agent channel exists here. A self-judgement would be RI-MTH03 'How we lose #1' with extra steps. The rule was written and SHA-256'd before any mapping.json was opened, has no free parameters, and its output cannot be influenced by what the critic knows. Packs left on disk for a round-2 judge.

method_deviations.deviation: Wrote three engine probes: critic-w1-library-consume.mjs (the three knowledge-gated resolutions, with a matched unread control), critic-w1-library-pages.mjs (all 65 books opened, page counts and words-per-page over every page, reported both including and excluding each book's final page), critic-w1-library-seam.mjs (all 60 topic-teaching books opened, topicsKnown before and after).
method_deviations.why: RI-UIX05 method step 2 requires opening every book via openMenu('book', id) and reading getUIState().book.pages, which no shipped tool did; and ARBITRATION §3's CONSUMPTION rule requires perturbing the model and observing an entity change behaviour, which no shipped tool does for books at all. Each probe carries its own control so a null result is distinguishable from a broken instrument — the consume probe's control is the unread run, and the seam probe's control is topicsKnown before any book is opened.

method_deviations.deviation: Broke both of the builder's new tools with mutations they do not run: (a) a derangement of the corpus that swaps every book's text with another book's while leaving every other field in place, (b) setting argonian_authored: true on all 65 books without touching a byline. Neither tool goes red on either.
method_deviations.why: TOOL-LOOP rule 3 q2. Both tools' own --self-test mutations perturb exactly the field the check reads, which makes them tautologies. The derangement is the mutation that distinguishes a check on the register from a check on the writing, and RI-LOR03 is an item about writing.

method_deviations.deviation: K2, K3, K5, K6, K7 and K10 were run by nobody — not by the builder and not by this critic — and are scored unmeasurable => 0 rather than argued from structure or borrowed from the content item.
method_deviations.why: The item is explicit: 'Unimplemented scores 0 ... a critic must not borrow RI-LOR03's score to cover it.' These six need a PNG sample of the reading screen at three resolutions, a frame-accurate input trace, a save/load round trip and an art-neutralised blind pair. They are the round-2 measurement list and they depress this score for a reason that is partly the corpus's rather than the builder's.

self_audit.self_audit_note: `ran_every_assigned_method` is false and the exceptions are named: RI-UIX05 K2, K3, K5, K6, K7 and K10 were run by nobody and are scored unmeasurable => 0. `blind_done_where_required` is false and this is the honest entry — RI-MTH03 M2 cannot be satisfied by a critic that assembled its own packs, so the blind JUDGEMENT is void and the separability finding rests on a pre-registered arithmetic rule plus a corpus-wide measurement, both of which are stated as such and neither of which is presented as a blind result. Every engine number was taken in a real browser at 320x240 with setRenderRate(0), with boot-check PASS before and after; loadavg was 2.18-12.77 and the one reading taken at 12.77 (the seam probe) is a boolean over an empty set, not a timing, so the load does not distort it. No source file was read to establish a fact: the consumption failure was measured first and traced afterwards, and the trace is offered as the remedy's address rather than as the evidence. The claim I attacked hardest and could not break is the writing itself — I read thirteen books end to end looking for the omniscient narrator RI-LOR03 exists to catch and did not find it, and I have said so at length rather than burying it under the failure.

notes: Nothing was committed. Three probes and one analysis tool were added to the working tree (tools/harness/critic-w1-library-{consume,pages,seam}.mjs, tools/uesp/mw-book-stats.py) along with four blind packs under reports/packs/ and their sibling reveal directories. The tree was being modified by other agents concurrently; the commit sha recorded is HEAD at the time of the engine runs.
